name: Road of the Hive (Dark Ages, Baali)

pages.name: Road of the Hive (Dark Ages, Baali)

text.content:
Latin name: Via Hyron

Via Hyron was the original Road developed by the Baali, and the most faithful to the bloodline's original ethos still follow it. As the Baali have extended their corruption across the continents, variations in the Road's exact tenets have cropped up, but the central message remains the same. An old Bedouin adage best describes its heart: My tribe and I against our enemies; my brother and I against all others. Despite the frequency with which members of the bloodline are at loggerheads, this Road urges its followers to combat the Beast through unity and tribal support — an individual who succumbs to his Beast is of no use for the Great Works the Baali aspire to, and so it is only prudent for individual Baali to help each other with their struggles.

Among followers of the Road of the Hive, loyalty is strongest between partners and Blood-Oathbound individuals. Following that, a Baali offers it to those within his nest, then to Baali of his same order, and finally to the bloodline as a whole. As the years pass, loyalty to peers has become as important as loyalty to one's order or to the Baali as a whole; some older Baali see this evolution as the beginning of the end for the Road, while others postulate that loyalty across the lines of the various orders will strengthen the bloodline's ability to function as one in a crisis.

Azaneal's revolt against the elders of the bloodline is one of the most damaging consequences of this fracture: a devotee of Via Diabolis (the Road of the Devil), Azaneal teaches his followers the precepts of the angellis ater rather than Via Hyron, meaning his Baali have no loyalty to the rest of the bloodline — only to themselves and to him.

Hierarchy of Sins (most to least severe; Conviction score needed to resist wrongdoing):

  1. (10) Arguing with a fellow follower of the Road.
  2. (9) Taking an outsider's side against that of another on the Via Hyron.
  3. (8) Actively working against the plans of another on the Road.
  4. (7) Actively working against a member of your nest's plans.
  5. (6) Betraying a fellow Baali.
  6. (5) Betraying a fellow traveler on the Road.
  7. (4) Betraying a member of your generation or order.
  8. (3) Betraying a member of your nest.
  9. (2) Betraying an elder of the bloodline.
  10. (1) Betraying your Sire or a Baali to whom you are Blood-Oathbound.

The higher a follower progresses on this hierarchy, the more difficult it becomes to refuse aid to another Baali — some have likened the Baali to a swarm of bees, and Via Hyron to a mandate for multiple queens.

vtmlarp.source: Clanbook: Baali, Chapter Three: Descent into Darkness
